subject.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)

question: Should OpenClaw treat a full-line bare, unnamespaced `<invoke name="…">…</invoke>` block as disposable malformed tool output even though current behavior preserves it as visible text?
rationale: The syntax is indistinguishable from a legitimate unfenced XML example, and the PR changes an existing visible-text and persistence contract rather than only adding support for namespace-qualified proxy output.

options.title: Restrict the new scrubber to named namespaces
options.body: Scrub `antml:` and `mm:` invoke blocks while keeping bare invoke support limited to already-established wrapper contexts, preserving current bare-example behavior.

options.title: Accept bare-block removal
options.body: Approve deletion of all standalone bare invoke blocks as a deliberate safety policy and require explicit upgrade-facing tests and release context for that contract change.

recommendation.title: Restrict the new scrubber to named namespaces
recommendation.body: Scrub `antml:` and `mm:` invoke blocks while keeping bare invoke support limited to already-established wrapper contexts, preserving current bare-example behavior.
